title: TS SDK: switchable stream sinks for async iterator <-> WebStream compatibility and robust retry semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Provide a single ergonomic TypeScript SDK surface that lets callers consume streamed model outputs as either async-iterators or Web Streams interchangeably, with deterministic retry semantics (idempotency + resume tokens) and sensible backpressure behavior. This ticket designs and implements a 'switchable sink' adapter that can present the same source as an AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array> or a ReadableStream, plus guidance and examples for application patterns.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a single streaming response object with methods: .asAsyncIterator(), .asWebStream()
Switching between consumers after partial consumption should be explicitly disallowed or documented as error; documented semantics for .tee() / multiplexing must be provided
Retryable transient errors (5xx, network) should attempt resume using server-provided resume_token when available; otherwise full retry with idempotency token
Backpressure honors underlying runtime: async-iterator pull rate vs ReadableStream byte consumer should not deadlock
Unit + integration tests covering consumer switch errors, resume-token flow, and stress scenarios
Documentation page with small code examples for both consumption styles and migration guidance
Benchmark demonstrating <10% overhead vs current raw streaming binding in a 99th percentile latency workload
design_notes: Implement StreamResponse wrapper around low-level transport that holds a single source subscription and exposes two facades: AsyncIteratorFacade and WebStreamFacade

Facade creation is lazy; both facades share an internal queue with backpressure signals. Only one facade may be actively pulling — creating second facade throws unless caller uses explicit .tee() API which creates clones with copy-on-write buffering and documented memory/cost trade-offs

Retry approach: prefer resume_token issued by model runtime. On resume, the SDK will request continuation from token and reapply any local prefix cache. If no token, do a full-request retry with idempotency_key header (generated/propagated from request metadata)
Expose configuration knobs: retry.max_attempts, retry.backoff_base_ms, consume.mode (single|teeable), buffering.window_ms to limit memory

Backpressure integration: use push/pull queue sized by tokens (approx tokens/bytes). For Node/deno, map ReadableStream default highWaterMark to internal limits; for browsers, rely on stream controller.desiredSize when available
Edge cases: streaming JSON chunks (structured output) require the same semantics; parsers must be able to pause/resume; we'll include helpers like parseNDJSON and combinePrefixCache
Compatibility: Node >= 18 native streams and Web Streams; provide a small polyfill helper for older runtimes that maps Node stream -> Web Stream via minimal shim
tradeoffs: Allowing multiple active consumers complicates memory and semantics; chosen default: single active consumer to keep semantics simple and avoid hard-to-debug duplication
Implementing .tee() increases memory and CPU cost; document as advanced and disabled by default
Resume-token correctness depends on server guarantees. The SDK will surface resume_token to apps for debugging but not rely on it for perfect at-least-once dedup without server guarantees
Tighter backpressure (small queue sizes) reduces latency but increases risk of stalls for slow consumers; default favors reliability with moderate buffer sizes
implementation_plan: 1) Add StreamResponse type in core transport layer with internal AsyncQueue and state machine
2) Implement AsyncIteratorFacade + unit tests for iteration lifecycle, cancel, throw
3) Implement WebStreamFacade using ReadableStream constructor; ensure controller.signal cancels underlying subscription
4) Add resume_token handling to transport retry middleware and wire idempotency_key header generation
5) Add .tee() as opt-in utility with explicit doc block and example
7) Docs + migration guide + examples repo PR
8) Benchmark and performance tune; adjust buffer defaults
9) Release notes and deprecation warnings for any existing streaming APIs we replace
test_plan: Integration: simulate transient transport disconnect with resume_token present; assert resumed stream continues from token and no duplicate chunks seen
Switch-consumer test: creating second facade without tee should throw; tee clones should receive equivalent data
Backpressure stress: run with slow consumer under heavy throughput and verify memory usage bounded
Browser/Node cross-compat: run in CI matrix (node 18/20, deno latest, chromium headless)
Fuzz tests: chunk boundary permutations (split tokens, truncated utf8) and ensure parsers handle reassembly
Performance tests: compare baseline raw binding vs wrapper at 95/99/99.9th percentiles
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag 'ts_stream_switchable_sinks' and land in canary channel
Invite 3 internal teams (console, dedicated-control-plane, samples) to test examples and provide feedback
After canary stability (1 week) flip feature flag and deprecate older streaming helper exports with a 2-release window
Announce in SDK changelog, highlight migration steps and provide automated codemods for common patterns
Monitor error rates and consumer feedback for 2 weeks post-release; be ready to roll back via feature flag
